methods.name: initialize
methods.description: Initialize once before other requests. Unsupported u32 versions return -32002; repeated initialization returns -32009 after parameter validation.

methods.name: sessions.status
methods.description: Report this sandbox, its activity, attachment and fixed policy. Host-only paths, identities and sockets are excluded; its worktree path remains visible.

methods.name: sessions.set-state
methods.description: Report provider-neutral activity; this does not change sandbox lifecycle.

methods.name: sessions.set-variables
methods.description: Update 1–16 history variables atomically. Empty values remove keys; values are at most 256 UTF-8 bytes without control characters.

methods.name: sessions.set-worktree
methods.description: Record or clear the caller worktree. Missing/null name clears; a non-null name must identify a real worktree under its configured folder.

methods.name: sessions.list
methods.description: List currently controlled members whose runtime has not been released, in daemon order. Released-but-retained sessions are excluded; a retiring member can still report a stopped lifecycle state. Host-only fields are excluded.

methods.name: sessions.get
methods.description: Read a session by immutable id or live agent name. The sandbox can read only members it controls; host-only fields are excluded.

errors.message: Record absent or no longer retained

methods.name: sessions.start
methods.description: Accept a member launch in the caller-owned raid with its fixed policy, workspace and launch options.

errors.message: Record absent or no longer retained

methods.name: sessions.stop
methods.description: Request teardown of a currently controlled member; authority is rechecked for every call.

errors.message: Record absent or no longer retained

methods.name: sessions.detach
methods.description: Detach this sandbox terminal and close the connection after replying; it cannot select another sandbox.

methods.name: targets.list
methods.description: List allowed run configurations in caller allowlist order, omitting missing current-manifest targets; requires a known manifest.

methods.name: terminals.create
methods.description: Host create accepts ordered positional parameters session,argv,cwd,env,name,rows,cols,notify or a closed named object; only session is required. Sandbox create/list/close accept a closed named object or null-as-empty, never positional arrays, and may never supply session. The existing sandbox relay derives the session from the connection and preserves policy/refusal ordering. Host notify=true is rejected before command/name/size validation; sandbox notify may request an exit notice. Size defaults independently to 40 rows and 120 columns. Command/name/size, target/policy/init, capacity and uniqueness checks precede canonical init encoding and spawn transfer.

methods.name: terminals.list
methods.description: Terminal records expose id, nullable name, display label, host/agent origin, Unix-millisecond started_at, rows/cols and attached. IDs increase per session and are never reused; list orders started terminals oldest first, including host and agent origins. Creation answers only after Spawned; pending creates do not appear in lists. Listed records remain until the program ends. Snapshots retain their domain record bridge until C15.

methods.name: terminals.close
methods.description: Close requests cancellation of the terminal process group and returns accepted=true. The entry remains until exit. Sandbox callers can close only agent-created terminals; host-created ones return -32009. An explicit close suppresses exit notices; disconnect while creating does not cancel the already requested terminal. Existing lifecycle/notice ownership stays handwritten.

methods.name: terminals.read
methods.description: Read/send/wait first validate command-specific input, then resolve a live session/terminal; pending waits remain connection-owned, count toward the per-session limit of 16 and are withdrawn on disconnect. A connection serves no other call while waiting. Host detach ends only the frontend and keeps the program alive; the frontend stream remains reserved until it closes. Resize validates 1..500 rows/cols before target resolution and updates the existing screen/PTY through runtime commands. Sandbox attach/detach/resize remain unavailable and never enter its callable allowlist. Host read/send/wait accept named objects or positional arrays in their field order: session,terminal then source,lines for read; text,keys for send; match,regex,exit,timeout,lines for wait. Only session and terminal are required structurally. Sandbox calls omit session and retain object-only/null-as-empty rules. Send needs a string text (even empty) or nonempty keys; empty/null text and keys are distinguished. Wait selects one nonempty match string, Rust regex string, or exit=true; match/regex allow exit absent/null/false. Source, line/timeout/text/key bounds and regex compilation remain existing semantic validators in their original order. Request constraints separately describe cross-field requirements without changing generated record/default decoding. Read returns text,alternate_screen,rows,cols and optional truncated=true. Wait returns matched+line, timeout, or exited+nullable code/signal+text; truncated=true is present only when output is cut. Matching final output precedes exit reporting. Existing 256 KiB text and 4 KiB line limits remain. Legacy CLI readers independently normalize string text/status/line and signed 64-bit code/signal; missing/malformed/non-object values retain their old fallback, with unknown wait status reported as timeout. Send/detach/resize callers ignore successful result bodies. Current producers use generated precise DTOs; private runtime relays stay JSON until their owning migration.

methods.name: devshell.lock
methods.description: Read this sandbox’s current trusted dev shell lock without evaluation or mutation. The existing empty-struct decoder accepts {} and []; null is refused. A dev shell is required.

errors.message: Invalid parameters or missing dev shell

methods.name: flake.run
methods.description: Build an app from this sandbox’s trusted dev shell generation, mount its closure, and return its program. No new trust or approval is granted. App attributes are bounded ASCII names. Evaluation is bounded by the daemon; disconnect cancels work. The client has no response timeout and runs only an existing normalized store file. Trailing input is refused before parameter/policy validation.

errors.message: Invalid parameters or missing dev shell

methods.name: devshell.diff
methods.description: Evaluate a read-only refresh preview. No approval request, candidate, GC root, mount or generation is changed; pending refresh candidates are left alone. Update and lock are mutually exclusive only when update is a non-null array and lock=true. Empty update means all inputs, absent/null update means no update. Requests accept named fields or [update,lock] with defaults, never null. Policy, trusted lock sources, evaluator limits and cancellation retain their existing order and ownership. Requires devshell-diff feature; client has no response timeout. Trailing input is refused before parameter and policy validation.

methods.name: editor.open
methods.description: Open sandbox files in the configured host Emacs. Requires editor-open feature and editor policy. Requests are named or [files,wait]; each file also retains [path,line?,column?] with the original order/defaults. The generated DTO is the named representation; nested positional metadata normalizes wire arrays before decoding. Semantic file/position checks remain in the gate before policy; trailing input is refused first. The daemon derives every TRAMP filename and pins that host to the requesting session and daemon before opening, without a shell. At most eight pending edits per sandbox. Disconnect kills/reaps the editor client; stopping the goblin returns -32009. No response deadline is imposed by the CLI.

errors.message: Missing editor policy, spawn failure or stopped session

methods.name: permissions.request
methods.description: Request a package, Docker engine, dev shell refresh or approved host command. Requires initialized, live caller authority; trailing input is refused before structural/semantic and policy checks. Body limit is 16384 bytes. Reasons are 1..1024 Unicode characters, not UTF-8 bytes. Named package defaults to empty; positional [kind,package,reason,update?,lock?,host?] requires the first three slots. Host commands retain nested [argv,cwd,env?,timeout?,detach?,name?] forms. Existing validators enforce kind-specific combinations, host-name diagnostics before general validity, command byte totals and policy/refusal order. Approval and completion are distinct; disconnect withdraws an attached request or cancels its host job, while detached host work survives and reports by notice. The daemon owns host path resolution/pinning, approvals, candidate identity and all descriptor/lifecycle state.

errors.message: Invalid request, host name, path or size
Policy, stale/liveness, grant or preparation conflict

x-client-result-profiles.name: grant-cli
x-client-result-profiles.description: The package/Docker/devshell CLI uses its original closed grant decoder, accepting named missing message or exactly [request,status,message], then requiring identifier request and ready/denied/error status. It emits message:null when absent. Unknown result fields, failed/withdrawn statuses and malformed types retain outcome-unknown exit 2.

methods.name: host.list
methods.description: List retained host-command records in insertion order, including finalized jobs. Sandbox visibility is limited to the calling session; another session job and a non-host permission are indistinguishable from an absent job (-32004). The CLI prints original JSON for list/status/cancel; wait/logs use independent status/outcome fields. Both routes require initialization and retain existing shutdown/liveness, capacity and cancellation ordering. Request bodies retain the endpoint 4096-byte limit. Active/no-outcome views always include eight fields, including nullable message/name/started_at; cached terminal views additionally include nullable exit_code/signal/code together. The record state, name and timestamp override cached outcome display fields, while log remains the sandbox path. Client readers preserve legacy independent field fallbacks or ignored bodies.

methods.name: raids.create
methods.description: Create a named raid with the authenticated caller as owner. Name validation and existing membership/creation rules stay in the pure domain before commit. Sandbox parameter shapes differ from host methods. Named params are closed; original positional forms are retained and null params refused. Existing initialization/stopping, runtime liveness, created-member control, actor derivation, event capacity and 4096-byte body limit remain in force. No capability or authority moves into generated DTOs.

methods.name: raids.leave
methods.description: Leave the caller raid. A non-owner created by a raid owner cannot leave while its creation relationship holds; owners may leave and pause remaining members. The last member dissolves the raid. No caller-supplied target/raid is accepted. Sandbox parameter shapes differ from host methods. Named params are closed; original positional forms are retained and null params refused. Existing initialization/stopping, runtime liveness, created-member control, actor derivation, event capacity and 4096-byte body limit remain in force. No capability or authority moves into generated DTOs.

methods.name: messages.send
methods.description: Authenticated sandbox mailbox mutation. Closed named parameters and original positional forms; null params refused. The caller-chosen key identifies an exact retry, recovered before target/liveness resolution. Caller identity never comes from parameters. Existing semantic validation keeps 1..64 ASCII identifier keys/IDs, positive claim generations, recipient/reason limits of 512 UTF-8 bytes, and bodies (including empty strings) up to 8192 UTF-8 bytes (schema x-max-bytes records these limits; runtime semantic enforcement stays handwritten, including escaped JSON). Each request uses the existing 65536-byte frame limit. Shared unpaused logged raid membership authorizes goblin routes, while host routes remain independent. Audit acceptance precedes publication; stale claims, capacity, audit failures, no-reply notices, name reuse, and deterministic retry behavior stay in the state machine. Successful CLI bodies remain uninterpreted and are printed unchanged, with the local operation key added only by the CLI. Send CLI omits absent conversation; raw API accepts absent/null conversation.

errors.message: Invalid mutation parameters or semantic values
Stale/conflicting claim, refused routing or audit failure

x-notifications.name: host.submitted
x-notifications.description: For attached permissions.request host-command work, the daemon sends this notification after the request is registered and before its terminal result. It identifies the sandbox output file. Detached submissions return pending acceptance and do not emit this notification. The host CLI legacy reader classifies by method only, even for nonstandard envelopes, and independently reads a string params.request or an empty string fallback. Preserve that behavior separately from the canonical closed producer params.
